texts.li: {X_nameDef} weighed out some of {X_possessive} goods for {A_nameDef}, then showed {A_objective} how to tell an honest scale from a crooked one: check it empty first, then swap the loads from one side to the other.

[theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} let {A_nameDef} hold the beam of {X_possessive} scales, and showed {A_objective} how a dishonest trader files a stone weight light, and how to catch it by weighing one stone against another.
[theirHightech] {X_nameDef} showed {A_nameDef} how a spring balance can be set to read heavy, and how to check one against a weight you already know.
{A_nameDef} watched {X_nameDef} count out a pile of silver by weight instead of coin by coin. {X_nameDef} explained how it is done, and how to check that it is done honestly.

{X_nameDef} of {FACTION} sat down at a table with {A_nameDef}, and before anything else said the words {X_possessive} people say over a meal: thanks for the food and for the hands that made it. {A_nameDef} waited until {X_pronoun} had finished.

[theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} sat down at a table with {A_nameDef} and first said a few words over it, the way {X_possessive} people always do. When {A_nameDef} asked, {X_pronoun} said they give thanks to the land and to the people who worked it.

[theirHightech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} sat down at a table with {A_nameDef} and said a short grace, the one {X_possessive} town says at its long tables. {X_pronoun} told {A_nameDef} it is said for the people who are not at the table.

[evening] At supper time {X_nameDef} sat down at a table with {A_nameDef} and said {X_possessive} people's words of thanks. {A_nameDef} asked what they meant, and {X_nameDef} explained them one by one.

li.label: an hour at the table with {X_nameDef}

ColonyCouncil.EncounterDef.label: a wild animal in the weather

texts.li: [rain] {A_nameDef} came on {X_indefinite} standing still in the rain, and went up closer than was wise to get a good look at {X_objective}.
[snow] {A_nameDef} saw {X_indefinite} out in the falling snow and walked closer than was wise to look at {X_objective}.
[storm] In the storm, {A_nameDef} found {X_indefinite} standing still, and went up close to see whether {X_pronoun} was hurt.
{A_nameDef} went closer than was wise to {X_indefinite} that was waiting out the weather, wanting a better look.

{X_nameDef} of {FACTION} asked {A_nameDef} where the colony cuts its wood, and told {A_objective} how {X_possessive} people choose which trees to fell: thin the young ones, and leave the old trees and the best seed trees standing.
[theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} that {X_possessive} people never fell the oldest tree in a wood. They cut a mark in its bark so that nobody does it by mistake.
[theirHightech] {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} how the foresters of {FACTION} number the trees in their woods on a chart and cut only so many each year, so there is always timber.
[winter] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} told {A_nameDef} that winter is the time to fell, when the sap is down and the wood dries straight.
{X_nameDef} of {FACTION} went over to the bench where the colony makes its clothes and looked it over, then showed {A_nameDef} a weave {X_possessive} people use that keeps the wind out.
{X_nameDef} looked over the colony's tailoring bench and showed {A_nameDef} how {X_possessive} people sew a seam that keeps the rain out.
[theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} went to the colony's bench, ran a hand over the cloth on it, and showed {A_nameDef} the twill {X_possessive} people weave, which wears twice as long.

[theirHightech] {X_nameDef} looked over the colony's bench and told {A_nameDef} that most of {X_possessive} people's cloth is made by machine, then showed {A_objective} a hand stitch {X_pronoun} had learned from an old tailor.
{X_nameDef} of {FACTION} saw {A_nameDef} squinting and showed {A_objective} how {X_possessive} people keep the glare of the snow out of their eyes, with a strip of cloth cut with two narrow slits.
[theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} showed {A_nameDef} the goggles {X_possessive} people carve from bone or wood, with a slit to look through, and how to make a pair.
[theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} rubbed a little soot under {A_nameDef}'s eyes against the glare, the way {X_possessive} people do on the snowfields.

[theirHightech] {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} that on {X_possessive} people's snowfields everyone wears a tinted visor, and showed {A_objective} how to make do with a strip of dark cloth until the colony has some.

{X_nameDef} of {FACTION} asked {A_nameDef} whether the colony has dug into the rock, and told {A_objective} how {X_possessive} people tell sound rock from rock that will fall: by the cracks, and by the damp coming through.
[theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} that {X_possessive} people tap the rock with a hammer before they dig into it. Sound rock rings, {X_pronoun} said, and rotten rock thuds.
[theirHightech] {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} how the miners of {FACTION} read the rock with a meter before they dig, and how to tell the same thing by eye when there is no meter.
{X_nameDef}, whose people dig for a living, told {A_nameDef} never to dig under a crack that is wet, and where to put the supports in a long tunnel.

With no river or ridge to mark it, {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} asked {A_nameDef} where the colony counts its land as ending. They talked it over and agreed that the old track was a fair line, and that each would tell their own people.
{X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} where the colony's land ends and {FACTION}'s grazing begins. They settled on a line of stones both of them knew, and shook hands on it.

[theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} that among {X_possessive} people the edge of a grazing is marked by a cairn, and asked where the colony's edge was. They agreed on a place, and {X_nameDef} said {X_pronoun} would tell the elders.
[theirHightech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} asked {A_nameDef} whether the colony had ever marked its boundary. Neither of them had a map, so they agreed on the old track as the line and wrote it down.
